Jane — thanks for sending this over and for a clear summary. Looping in legal (Kimberly), finance (Karthik) and account lead (Mina) to coordinate redlines and evidence. Quick internal notes so everyone is aligned before we circulate a marked-up order form: 

- Consolidated invoicing: we typically invoice the contracting entity on the order form. We can support consolidated billing in some cases but need entity-level tax evidence for remittance (VAT ID, local registration).
- Net terms: our standard is Net 30. For larger committed TCV we have flexibility to extend to Net 45 or Net 60 conditioned on credit checks and an approved PO cadence.
- Withholding: in jurisdictions with mandatory withholding we ask customers to provide evidence and will either gross-up or provide an offset credit depending on the jurisdiction and netting rules. For EU customers we generally handle VAT via our EU entity; withholding is uncommon but we need clarity for local subsidiaries.

Action items for Redwood team:
- Kimberly: propose precise redline language for invoices/entities/gross-up and a fallback where withholding applies.
- Karthik: confirm invoicing cadence options and whether finance can accept Net 60 under credit approvals; outline any additional billing evidence we need.
- Mina: I will coordinate with the customer on PO timing and whether they can provide VAT cert + entity remittance target.

Jane — can you share Acme's preferred billing entity and the PO (if available)? If we can get the PO and VAT cert this week we should be able to return a tracked-redline by Monday.

Thanks,
Sofia Ivanova
Enterprise Account Lead | Redwood Inference
sofia_ivanova@redwood.com

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>

Date: Sun, 12 Sep 2026 08:41:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Order Form and commercial schedule — draft redlines and evidence request

Thanks, Sofia and Jane. I reviewed OrderForm_v3 and drafted tracked redlines (redline_orderform_trackchanges.docx). High level guidance and proposed wording below to keep the conversation moving: 

1) Invoicing & billing entity (proposed new section):
"Invoices shall be issued to the Billing Entity specified on the Order Form. Where Customer requests consolidated invoicing for multiple Customer entities, Customer shall provide written instruction and valid tax identifiers for each entity; Redwood will rely on those instructions and invoice the specified Billing Entity unless otherwise agreed in writing."

2) Net terms (proposed compromise):
"Standard payment terms are Net 30. For Order Forms with committed annual spend >= EUR 500,000 Redwood may agree to Net 45 or Net 60 upon completion of a credit review and provision of a purchase order referencing the Order Form. Any extended terms will be documented in an amendment."

3) Withholding & gross-up:
"If withholding tax is required by applicable law, Customer shall provide documentation of the withholding requirement and file evidence of payment to the relevant tax authority. Where withholding applies and Customer is unable to obtain relief at source, Redwood and Customer will negotiate a mutually acceptable measure (e.g., gross-up, credit, or price adjustment) to ensure Redwood receives the agreed net consideration)."

4) VAT and tax evidence: request copies of VAT registration or tax-residency certificates where Customer requests invoicing to a specific EU entity. For non-EU entities, request W-8/W-9 as applicable.

5) PO and remittance: require that any PO referencing the Order Form include the billing entity and payment terms; otherwise invoices will be processed under the Order Form terms.

Attachments included: redline_orderform_trackchanges.docx (proposed edited document with track changes)

Notes for finance: Karthik, please confirm if finance can provisionally accept Net 60 for this account pending credit check, and whether we should include an escrow/retention clause if withholding could materially impact cash flow (e.g., >5% withholding).

Jane, if Acme can provide PO_12345.pdf and the VAT cert for the EU entity, we can finalize redlines quickly. If you'd prefer a short call to run through the redlines, happy to join Monday morning.

Regards,
Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel | Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.com

Appreciate the quick turn, Kimberly. A few responses from procurement/legal at Acme: 

- We can provide PO_12345.pdf and the EU VAT certificate by end of day tomorrow.
- Acme's internal policy strongly prefers Net 60 for platform contracts unless there is an explicit early-pay discount; extending to Net 30 would require CFO sign-off. Is there any early-pay discount Redwood can offer (1-2% over 15 days)?
- Regarding withholding: our country teams indicate no withholding in the EU holding jurisdiction, but certain regional subsidiaries may have withholding — we'll flag those. We prefer a mutual process to handle country-level withholding rather than a universal gross-up.

We are happy to do a 30-minute call tomorrow to finalize. Suggested times: 09:00-10:00 or 14:00-15:00 CEST.
